1.why: Every MFA/recovery endpoint goes through owner(), which derives the account solely from session.userId (accounts.get(session.userId)) and never accepts a client-supplied identifier, so MFA settings are bound to the signed-in user.

2.why: Verification codes are scoped per session (session.identityCode) and TOTP codes derive from the account's own encrypted secret, so a code issued to one user does not work for any other user.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify only rotates the CSRF token and changes stage; the session token and any other concurrent sessions are never invalidated, so previous sessions continue to work.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted (mfaSecretEncrypted) and recovery codes are stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA-256 hashes (210k iterations), never in plaintext at rest.

5.why: All secrets, OTPs, tokens, and recovery codes are produced from crypto.getRandomValues via bytes()/randomChars() with modulo-bias rejection sampling, a cryptographically secure RNG.

6.why: The client keeps the CSRF token, secret, and codes only in in-memory variables (no localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB), and the only cookie, Host-mfa_session, is HttpOnly, so nothing sensitive sits in browser storage or readable cookies.

7.why: Server-side validators (validEmail, validOtp, validSecret, validRecovery, phone(), password length cap, JSON shape checks) validate and normalise all user-supplied input before use.

8.why: The SPA renders all dynamic values via textContent/createElement, the QR SVG innerHTML contains only integer coordinates, APIs return JSON, and a nonce-based CSP blocks injected script execution.

9.why: The server issues no redirects at all (no Location headers and navigation is a fixed client-side screen state machine), so open redirects are impossible, though no explicit redirect allow-list mechanism exists because none is needed.

10.why: All responses set CSP with per-request nonces and frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS (max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, plus Referrer- and Permissions-Policy.

11.why: The session cookie is set as 'Host-mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict', carrying all three required attributes.

12.why: Although server errors are generic with no stack traces, ACADEMIC_LOCALHOST_TEST_MODE is hardcoded true so live OTPs are returned in API responses (testingCode) and the client consoleSecret() writes OTPs, the authenticator code, and recovery codes to console logs.

13.why: Identity codes are marked used and cleared after success and expire after 10 minutes, TOTP codes are time-windowed with replay blocked via mfaLastCounter, and recovery codes are deleted from the account upon use.

14.why: Five failed identity, OTP, or recovery attempts trigger a 10-minute lockout and code requests are throttled to one per 20 seconds, but the counters are per-session and the password sign-in endpoint itself has no rate limiting.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a fresh token, sessions enforce 8-hour absolute and 20-minute idle timeouts in current(), and logout sets invalidated, deletes the session, and clears the cookie with Max-Age=0.
